personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: Swapping a line-by-line floor for a per-pixel renderer that runs every frame is the kind of change an agent gets subtly wrong, and nothing in the design yet says what it costs a frame on /play.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: Hills and a minimap in the arcade are polish on what I already see as a gimmick; at least it touches one folder and no data.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: Five asks from one sentence, shipped as one PRD: hills, boxes, a thick deck, tipping and a minimap make the race feel like a real kart game.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: It stays inside arcade/kart and keeps the race pure and seeded, which keeps it reviewable; I want the rivals' tuning held by a test, not by a lucky seed.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: Every point is something a player sees at once on the first lap: a quick, visible win.

objection.text: A per-pixel renderer written by an agent and run every frame is where slow frames and bugs reach production on /play. I want a guard that bounds its cost, not only colour tests.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: The floor's samples are capped and a test holds the cap at every waypoint on both grids; with depth and deck tests beside it, I can trust the renderer.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: No migration, no data, one revert to roll back: cheap enough that I do not mind the gimmick.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: Fifteen criteria anyone can check in one race, and MULTI gets the minimap for free.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: The rivals' three seeds are a test now, and the risk on best times is written down rather than discovered.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: The spec keeps the race players know, laps, items and the fall, and adds what they asked for on top.
